div.head: ECf 11.1 B 3
div.ab: Uicarius uero Dei estis in regno iuxta psalmistam regem: ‘Domini est terra et plenitudo eius orbis terrarum et uniuersi qui habitant in eo’; et rursum iuxta psalmistam regem: ‘Dilexisti iustitiam et odisti iniquitatem; propterea unxit te Deus Deus tuus oleo letitie pre consortibus tuis’; et rursum iuxta psalmistam regem: ‘Deus, iudicium tuum’ etc. Non enim dixit: ‘iudicium neque iustitiam Cesaris’.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 636 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

note.seg: psā the MSS always; prophetam Ld

div.ab: You are the vicar of God in the kingdom, according to the king the psalmist: ‘The earth is the Lord's and the fullness thereof, the world and all who dwell in it’; and again according to the king the psalmist: ‘You have loved justice and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows’; and again according to the king the psalmist: ‘O God, your judgment’ etc. For he did not say: ‘the judgment nor the justice of Caesar’.
